question: In CooperBench coop runs, where does the first coordination conflict happen, which kinds of conflict occur, and how does each agent handle them?

dev.name: s1_screen
dev.note: default CooperBench prompt; codebook and prompt checks

library.name: s1_main
library.note: default prompt; outcome is the official merge

library.name: s2_baseline
library.note: default prompt; outcome is after the llm re-merge of conflicted runs

conditions.name: s2_own_feature
conditions.note: agents told that overlapping edits are merged automatically

conflict_point: defined by the detector, not the labeler: the first sent message after which both agents have claimed the same file (a path both mention, or a reference to 'the same file'); per agent, the trajectory step where it has sent its own claim and received the partner's. 'exclusive' marks a request to stay out of the file before that point, the strict reading of section 2.2 of the benchmark plan

labeler.input: feature titles and every message in causal order, with delivery failures and exits; no code, patches, tests or outcomes

validation: a second independent label on 40 random library runs (Cohen's kappa per field); a hand check of 30 runs against the messages; the outcome analysis is exploratory and reported per set, since S1 and S2 score merges differently
outputs: runs/c_conflict_states/conflict_states.csv and conflict_summary.json; copies in results/ once the library is labeled
